behaviors.name: Acrobatic Roulade (Forward Roll)
behaviors.description: Dynamic forward somersault over the duck's head, rolling on its back and landing back onto its feet in a standing position.
behaviors.details: A high-agility maneuver demonstrating full-body dynamic balance and shock resilience. Trained in MuJoCo Warp with full contact physics (robot_allcollisions.xml). Shipped in the official Pollen Alpha stack and hot-swapped by robotd during an explicit rolling trigger window.

verification.summary: Verified on physical MicroDuck hardware on padded mats and carpet. Shipped in official MicroDuck release video montage.
verification.notes: Recommend performing on padded surface, yoga mat, or carpet to avoid cosmetic shell scratches.

behaviors.name: Alpha Dynamic Walk
behaviors.description: Standard bipedal walking gait with 50 Hz velocity tracking (vx, vy, yaw_rate) and active head-pose orientation control.
behaviors.details: The flagship locomotion policy for MicroDuck. Trained in MuJoCo Warp via mjlab and PPO using the BAM M6 actuator model for Dynamixel XL330 servos. Includes domain randomization on battery voltage, friction, and motor command delay. Exports a baked observation normalizer into the ONNX computational graph.

verification.summary: Verified on physical MicroDuck hardware with Rockchip RK3566 and 14 Dynamixel XL330 servos. Shipped as default walking policy.
verification.hardware_target: MicroDuck v1 (Rockchip RK3566, 14 Dynamixel XL330-M077, 2S LiPo)
verification.notes: Operates at 50 Hz control loop. Velocity envelope: -0.2 to +0.25 m/s forward/back, ±1.0 rad/s angular yaw rate.

contract.actuator_model: Dynamixel XL330 (BAM M6 voltage control law)

behaviors.name: Autonomous Ground Pick
behaviors.description: One-shot crouching behavior that reaches beak to the floor to pick up objects with its articulated mouth gripper, then smoothly returns to stand.
behaviors.details: Triggered via gamepad 'A' button or RPC call. Driven by a phase parameter [cos(2pi*t), sin(2pi*t), 0] fed into the velocity command channels over a 3.5-second gesture window. Coordinates beak opening, deep leg squat, and pitch compensation so the soft beak contacts the ground reliably without tipping.

verification.summary: Verified on physical MicroDuck hardware picking up objects from carpet and hard flooring with the beak gripper.
verification.hardware_target: MicroDuck v1 (Rockchip RK3566, 14 Dynamixel XL330-M077 + Beak Gripper)
verification.notes: Executes on 3.5s phase clock (phase advances 1/5.0 per sec, ends at 0.7 phase).

behaviors.name: Dynamic Fall Recovery
behaviors.description: Automatic fall recovery policy capable of restoring MicroDuck to standing posture from face-down, face-up, or sitting positions.
behaviors.details: Triggered automatically when the onboard IMU's projected gravity vector exceeds tilt thresholds (or commanded via gamepad recovery button). The policy executes robust arm-less biped pushups, righting the duck without human intervention before handing off control back to the standing/walking state machine.

verification.summary: Verified on physical MicroDuck hardware with fall detection triggers enabled. Robot self-rights after tip-over.
verification.hardware_target: MicroDuck v1 (Rockchip RK3566, 14 Dynamixel XL330-M077, 2S LiPo)
verification.notes: Requires full body contact physics. Uses robot_allcollisions.xml in simulation.

behaviors.description: Aerodynamic tuck crouch maneuver while coasting on roller skates, lowering center of gravity for high-speed stability.
behaviors.details: A 3.5-second one-shot gesture on rollers. Driven by phase encoding [cos(2pi*t), sin(2pi*t), 0] in the command slots (matching ground-pick architecture). The duck folds its legs, lowers its center of mass near the wheel axles, and smoothly returns to an upright skating tuck.

behaviors.name: Roller Skate Velocity Drive
behaviors.description: High-speed skating locomotion utilizing passive roller skate wheels mounted under the feet, featuring asymmetric velocity limits and turn rate damping.
behaviors.details: Converts MicroDuck into a mobile skating robot. When passive roller blade attachments are installed and D-pad up is held, robotd switches to the roller policy suite. Velocity profile allows up to +0.6 m/s forward acceleration and -0.5 m/s braking, with angular velocity clamped to 0.3 rad/s to prevent tipping.

verification.hardware_target: MicroDuck v1 + Roller Skate Accessories (passive bearings/wheels)

behaviors.name: Smooth Sit ↔ Stand
behaviors.description: Controlled bi-directional transition between upright standing and rested sitting posture with continuous head commandability.
behaviors.details: A unified policy trained in MuJoCo to handle both gentle sitting down and standing back up. Softens motor gains during transition to ensure the duck does not slam into the ground. While sitting, head orientation remains commandable through the 4-dim head pose observation slot.

verification.summary: Verified on physical MicroDuck hardware with gamepad Y button toggle. Robot smoothly sits down and stands back up.
verification.notes: Transition utilizes posture flags in twist magnitude; rise runs with softened standing gains.

behaviors.name: Standing 6-DOF Body Pose Controller
behaviors.description: Fine-grained torso orientation and height controller while standing, continuously mapping roll, pitch, yaw, and squat commands to compliant leg and neck adjustments.
behaviors.details: Developed for the community microduck_runtime port. Utilizes the full 6-dim body_pose command vector (tx, ty, tz, roll, pitch, yaw) in the standard 61-dim observation contract. Allows interactive puppeteering of the duck's stance height, torso tilt, and look-around angles without shifting foot contact locations.

verification.hardware_target: MicroDuck Raspberry Pi SBC / Dynamixel XL330

behaviors.name: Backlash-Compensated Walking
behaviors.description: Velocity-tracking walking policy trained specifically to withstand ±1° gear play (2° total) in series with every XL330 servo gearbox.
behaviors.details: Models mechanical gear lash explicitly via passive_<joint>_backlash hinges in the MJCF model (robot_*_backlash.xml). Because the physical Dynamixel encoder sits on the output side of the gear play, both the BAM firmware PD emulation and joint observations read directly through the backlash, resulting in extreme sim2real fidelity even on worn gearboxes.

verification.summary: Trained and verified with explicit ±1° backlash hinge physics and domain randomized friction.
verification.hardware_target: MicroDuck v1 (Dynamixel XL330 with gear train backlash)
verification.notes: Observation and action dimensions are strictly identical to standard 61-D contract.

media.caption: Backlash-compensated walking gait maintaining stability despite servo gear slop

behaviors.name: Classic Swizzle Skating
behaviors.description: Symmetric rhythmic swizzle gait on passive roller wheels, generating forward propulsion without lifting feet off the ground.
behaviors.details: Emulates human inline skating swizzles (hourglass foot patterns). Uses continuous lateral leg splaying and converging arcs to convert leg extension forces into forward rolling momentum without foot lift-off. Trained in mjlab using full roller wheel contacts.

verification.summary: Verified in MuJoCo Warp / mjlab simulation over 4096 parallel environments with BAM actuator friction physics.
verification.notes: Targeted for smooth surfaces like wood or polished concrete where passive wheel friction is minimal.

behaviors.details: Extends the baseline velocity policy with continuous heightfield domain randomization in MuJoCo Warp. Features higher foot clearance during the swing phase and aggressive compliance response when the leading foot strikes premature obstacles or depressions.

behaviors.name: Waddle Custom Locomotion
behaviors.description: Independent community-developed walking gait featuring a pronounced rhythmic waddling sway tuned for biped compliance.
behaviors.details: Developed by Nick Koenig (nickoenig37) as an exploration of duck-like biomimetic locomotion. Modifies reward terms on lateral torso oscillation and foot contact cadence to produce a distinctive waddle gait while preserving the standard 61-dim observation and 14-actuator contract.
